evals.prompt: Design a notification platform for our company. We have not provided traffic, delivery channels, latency, compliance, or reliability requirements. Give a production design.
evals.expected_output: Frame the missing requirements first. Ask only material questions or proceed with labeled assumptions, define non-goals and channel-specific SLOs, and avoid choosing infrastructure before scale and delivery semantics are known.

evals.prompt: Design image ingestion for 120 million uploads per month. Average image size is 4 MB, peak traffic is 8 times average, and originals are retained for 365 days. Show first-order request-rate, bandwidth, and storage estimates before selecting components.
evals.expected_output: Show unit-aware arithmetic: monthly uploads converted to average and peak requests per second, payload multiplied into bandwidth, and 365-day raw storage with overhead/replication stated separately. Label estimates and headroom rather than presenting false precision.

evals.prompt: Review an API design where a checkout request synchronously calls identity, pricing, inventory, fraud, payment, shipping, email, and analytics services with a 200 ms p99 target. Every client retries twice on timeout. Identify the main production risks and smallest corrections.
evals.expected_output: Identify impossible or unproven latency composition, availability multiplication, retry amplification, duplicate side effects, and a large synchronous blast radius. Keep only response-critical calls synchronous, set an end-to-end deadline and bounded retry budget, make effects idempotent, and move notifications/analytics asynchronously.

evals.prompt: Design consistency for limited-stock checkout. Customers must never receive confirmation for stock that was not reserved, reads may be a few seconds stale, payment authorization can time out and later succeed, and duplicate requests are common.
evals.expected_output: State the invariant and authoritative inventory owner, use atomic reservation with expected-state/version checks, use a stable idempotency key, distinguish payment timeout from failure, and define durable workflow/reconciliation and compensation for late outcomes.

evals.prompt: A 10-year-old monolith processes orders reliably but deploys slowly. Propose a migration to an independently scalable fulfillment capability without a big-bang rewrite or unsafe database dual writes.
evals.expected_output: Establish baseline and ownership, create compatible contracts, isolate the fulfillment boundary incrementally, use an Outbox or change capture rather than application dual writes, shadow or dual-read and reconcile, canary traffic, retain rollback compatibility, and define exit criteria before removing the old path.

evals.prompt: A new internal CRUD application expects 40 requests per second, one team, one PostgreSQL database, and no independently scaled workloads. The proposal starts with 14 microservices, Kafka, Kubernetes, a service mesh, and three caches for future scale. Review it.
evals.expected_output: Reject the speculative complexity. Recommend a modular monolith with one database and clear internal boundaries, identify concrete triggers for later extraction, and preserve observability, security, backups, and performance testing without deploying distributed infrastructure prematurely.
